There is a dire need to balance the law," says Swarup Sarkar, one of the founder members of Save Family Foundation.

Heading: Shrine row fed on Jammu-Valley’s history of divide - Indian Express
Content:
As Indore struggles to return to normalcy and victims' families try to come to grips with their losses, the ruling BJP and the main opposition party Congress are engaged in a vicious campaign blaming each other for turning the town into a tinderbox.

The commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh has witnessed several incidents of communal violence over the last couple of years. But it was for the first time since the riots that followed the Babri Masjid demolition that the entire town was brought under curfew again.

Congress leader Digvijay Singh, who was chief minister of the state for ten years, says when a chief minister wants, he can ensure that no communal riot takes place in the state. He promptly blamed the ruling party for the riots.

The Congress felt Chouhan's assertion that "the Jammu and Kashmir Government's decision on the land transfer (to the Amarnath shrine board) had insulted the majority community" only added fuel to the fire and signalled to the administration and police that they were supposed to go soft on elements involved in violence.

No wonder, the state's Director General of Police quote on record that "even God can't predict when a communal situation can be completely brought under control."

The BJP, for its part, blames the riots on the Congress, saying the Students' Islamic Movement of India prospered during its 10-year-long reign in the central Indian state. The ruling party is sure that the communal disturbances have been engineered by the proscribed students' organisation.

State BJP president Narendra Singh Tomar, despite five deaths on the day the Hindu organisations gave a call for Bharat Bandh, thanked the people of Madhya Pradesh for a successful bandh. He alleged that the Congress sponsored the latest riots to divert attention from the probe initiated by the state government into the activities of SIMI.

State BJP spokesman Umashankar Gupta was not so sure if the SIMI link had already been exhausted and said the Government would expose the role of SIMI and the support it got from the Congress.

Former BJP chief minister Uma Bharati, herself no stranger to communal riots, felt that criminal elements had infiltrated organisations like the Bajrang Dal "in recent times" and they can't be controlled once they are unleashed during these situations.

The stage for the war of words was set, it seemed, when BJP's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani's book was released in the state capital last week. Advani had managed the presence of spiritual guru Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Yoga guru Baba Ramdev on the dais. Both criticised the decision to revoke the land transfer to the shrine board.

While Advani himself avoided the mention of Amarnath, he said, while leaving Bhopal, that the UPA Government's decision was "anti-Hindu" and that it often succumbed to pressure from fundamentalists from other religions while taking the majority community for granted.

Heading: Eye on LS polls, Maya plans 1 lakh ‘free’ houses for poor - Indian Express
Content:
The turmoil over the Amarnath land issue may have ignited a communal cauldron in J-K and toppled the state Government, but the history of the divide between Kashmir and Jammu goes back to pre-Partition days. In fact, its seeds were sown in the 1930s with the Kashmiri uprising against the Dogra rule, which in 1947 culminated in the transfer of political power to the Muslim majority.

Though the Kashmiri movement against Maharaja Hari Singh wasn't essentially communal in nature, the fact that it was a predominantly Muslim uprising against a Hindu ruler from Jammu gave it a simultaneous regional religious dimension. And the loss of political power in the post-1947 democratic dispensation headed by Shiekh Abdullah only accentuated the divide. Jammu Dogras harboured a deep sense of political marginalisation which resulted in the growth of religious outfits like Praja Parishad in 1947.

The Parishad spearheaded the opposition to Kashmiri "dominance" in 1949. The outfit declared its opposition to the separate constitution and the national flag for Kashmir as also Article 370 which grants Kashmir a special status and forbids the owning of land by non-state subjects. The Parishad was also stridently opposed to Sheikh Abdullah's National Conference, which it thought only represented the aspirations of Kashmiri Muslims. The Sheikh was accused of Muslim-ising the state through his Kashmir-centric policies. In fact, the party was behind huge demonstrations in Jammu in the '50s when a National Conference flag was hoisted at a local college.

In 1970, the Praja Parishad merged with the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. But the very localised nature of the grievances in Jammu soon found expression in the growth of regional outfits like the Jammu Mukti Morcha. An apolitical organisation, the JMM stands for trifurcation of J-K. It believes that this is important to solve the Kashmir issue and end the sense of deprivation and identity crisis felt by the people of Jammu and Ladakh regions. The trifurcation of J-K, the party says, will not only localise the area of strife, but counter Pakistani propaganda that the entire state is in turmoil and that its entire population harbours a grudge against India. The JMM advocates statehood for Jammu and a Union Territory status for Ladakh.

Though Kashmir has also had its due share of religious parties, most prominent of them being the Jamaat-i-Islami, they usually define their politics more by a strident anti-India agenda rather than an anti-Jammu sentiment. The 1947 communal bloodbath in Jammu which resulted in the migration of a substantial number of Jammu Muslims to Pakistan has however been a sore point with the Jamaat-i-Islami and also separatist outfits.

The state Government has made some efforts to redress the regional grievances. The Ganjendragadkar and Sikri Commissions were set up to inquire into complaints of regional discrimination in 1967 and 1979 respectively. One result of the Ganjendragadkar commission was the division of Jammu and Kashmir University into separate Kashmir and Jammu universities.

The recent turbulence in the state, though essentially grounded in the Valley's separatist politics and its attendant complexities, ended up feeding into the old regional rivalry. While the resignation of the Ghulam Nabi Azad Government may have soothed frayed tempers, the Amarnath land issue is likely to assume a prime place in J-K's regional political discourse for some time and figure prominently in the coming Assembly elections.

Heading: UPA Govt insulted us, as for future you can guess: Karat - Indian Express
Content:
With an eye on the Lok Sabha elections, the Mayawati Government is planning to distribute one lakh houses to the urban poor — either free, or for a nominal price — this year. The matter is likely to be placed before the state Cabinet shortly.

The houses will be built under the Kanshi Ram Shahri Garib Awas Yojna, which Mayawati had announced last month on the anniversary of the formation of the first BSP Government in the state in 1995.

At that time, the Government had not stated what the beneficiaries of the scheme, meant for those below poverty line, would have to pay. According to the proposal, the structures will be compact two-room houses with a kitchen and a bathroom.

"The Government will construct one lakh houses for poor people every year. Each house, costing Rs 1.75 lakh, will be built in an area of 20 square metre," informed an official from the Urban Development Department.

The Government is formulating guidelines which, after getting a clearance from the Cabinet, will kickstart the scheme. The guildelines will address issues such as — how and from where the land will be arranged, which agencies will execute the work, what will be the criteria for the selection of beneficiaries, and whether the houses will be given free or a token price will be charged.

"It will be almost free as we are thinking of taking a nominal amount that could range between Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000. Charging the full cost would not be practical because the houses are meant for the poor who can't pay it," said an officer at the Chief Minister's Office.

The houses are to be built in phases, with 71 district headquarters to be taken up in the first phase. Town areas — Nagar Palika, Parishads and Nagar Panchayats — are to be covered in the second and third phases.

Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes will be given priority in allotment, with a special provision for the poor belonging to the upper castes, shelter-less widows and the handicapped.

This housing replaced the Kanshi Ram Shahri Samagra Vikas Yojna, which was announced by Mayawati herself on October 7 last year. That scheme aimed to provide basic facilities, like housing, clean drinking water, sewerage, drainage, road, cleanliness, health, employment and electrification to people living in urban areas.

Heading: All eyes on Speaker, party says his decision - Indian Express
Content:
Saying it was "insulted", the Left on Wednesday formally withdrew support to the UPA Government, clubbing price rise and economic policies with the Indo-US nuclear deal as reason for parting ways, and sought an immediate trust vote.

Minutes after the four Left parties submitted separate letters of withdrawal to President Pratibha Patil, CPM general secretary Prakash Karat ruled out any truck with the Congress in future and launched a scathing attack on the Government for pushing what he called a "notorious" and "dubious" nuclear deal.

The Left leaders urged the President to direct the Prime Minister to seek a vote of confidence in Lok Sabha "immediately" as they said the government has lost "majority and legitimacy" after their withdrawal of support. "The Congress-led government was supported by the Left parties on the basis of a commitment that it would follow an independent foreign policy in contrast to the pro-American stand of the BJP-led government. That commitment has been violated. Hence, the Left parties will have to dissociate from the government," they said.

Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party too approached the President and its general secretary, Amar Singh, submitted a letter pledging support of 39 party MPs to the government.

The Left will come out tomorrow with the notes exchanged with the government on the nuclear deal in the last 10 months, compiling them in a booklet.

After the formal separation, Karat said the government "insulted" the Left parties by not showing them the text of the draft IAEA safeguards agreement after agreeing to come back to the UPA-Left committee with it following negotiations with the IAEA secretariat.

"At all stages of the notorious nuclear deal, the Manmohan Singh government has not been transparent," he said, demanding that the text of the safeguards agreement be made public.

He claimed that while the Indian government has hidden from the people the draft of the safeguards agreement, the US has made public the draft of an additional protocol it is signing with the IAEA. "The government and Manmohan Singh always look up to America. There are some things they should learn," he said.

Asked whether the Left would have any ties with the Congress in future, Karat said "after today's decision, it should be clear to you what relationship we will have (with them) in the future."

On efforts by the Congress to save the government, he said "knowing the Congress well, we know they will do anything to remain in power. Let them try."

Karat said the government had plunged the country into a political crisis when people were groaning under price rise and double-digit inflation.

"By pursuing a neo-liberal agenda, the Congress-led government is following the same policies of the previous BJP government. These policies are squarely responsible for the distressing spectacle of agrarian crisis, farmers' suicides, mass poverty, price rise and unemployment," he said.

"We had told the Prime Minister and the government to take certain urgent measures (to tackle inflation). All our five demands were rejected. We cannot be party to a government which is callous to the sufferings of the people and whose priority is to fulfill its commitment to US President George Bush and not to the people of India," he said.

He accused the government of "disregarding" Parliament on the nuclear issue as discussions in both the Houses had shown that the majority was against the deal and of "violating" the November 16, 2007 understanding that the next step on the deal would be taken only after the panel finalised its findings.

Karat ridiculed External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's assertion that the text of the IAEA draft was classified. "Who has declared it a classified document. Is it the UPA government's decision or that of the IAEA secretariat?" he asked.

Referring to the US making public the protocol it was currently discussing with the IAEA, he said "Are we to believe that the IAEA has one standard for the US and another standard for India? No text is confidential at the IAEA unless the government concerned wants it to be. The text has to be made public. Nuclear scientists, experts and people should have access to the document," he said.

Heading: NDA presents united front, gears up to vote against Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam: The MDMK, an erstwhile minor partner of the UPA, has announced that it will not support the Indo-US nuclear deal as it harms sovereignty of the country. The decision to vote against the issue, announced by party leader Vaiko at Chennai on Wednesday, was not surprising as the party was ousted from the Central alliance after it decided to go with the AIADMK, arch rival of the DMK, in the last Assembly polls. "If the deal is signed, India will be surrendering its nuclear independence to that country," Vaiko said.

Lalu on Nitish for his volte-face on deal: Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav on Wednesday hit out at Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's "volte-face" on the nuclear deal. Speaking at a function here, the RJD president asked: "I wonder if it was the same Nitish Kumar who had vouched for a nuclear power plant at Nalanda during his early days as CM?" He added that the "Left's withdrawal of support at this juncture is like pulling the chain of the development train". Although the UPA is proverbially and literally "left" in the lurch, the RJD chief made his 'affection' for the Left parties clear, describing the recent break at the Centre as "lost love".

Sikkim Democratic Front: The SDF on Wednesday endorsed the Indo-US civilian nuclear deal stating that the agreement would "enable our country to generate nuclear energy in the years to come". "We fully stand by the Prime Minister and the nuclear deal and would accordingly support the confidence vote to be moved by the Prime Minister in the Lok Sabha whenever he decides to seek it," Sikkim Chief Minister Pawan Kumar Chamling said here.

Heading: SP says flock intact, meets President - Indian Express
Content:
As expected, the National Democratic Alliance will vote against a trust motion brought in by the UPA Government.

"The NDA is united and will vote against the Government if it introduces a vote of confidence," said BJP leader Sushma Swaraj on Wednesday after attending a meeting of NDA allies. She, however, alleged that the Government had created confusion "by not announcing a special session".

"The CCPA has announced the dates of the monsoon session starting from August 11. There was no announcement of a special session though. The two are different," she said. The BJP reiterated that the special session should be ideally held within the next five to six days.

While the BJP-led alliance was happy with all its allies except the Trinamool Congress, who they still consider an ally. Though the allies were present at the NDA meet, it doesn't expect any miracles in the trust vote. The BJP feels that while smaller parties would be guided by their own compulsions rather than the nuclear debate during the voting, the party wouldn't like the trust vote to be reduced to a vote "for or against the nuclear deal".

"The UPA should be pinned on issues like the price rise and the internal security situation apart from its mishandling of the Amarnath Yatra. We wouldn't allow the trust vote to be reduced to a single issue. Also, the longer the government survives, the more acute the anti-incumbency sentiment against the Government," claimed a BJP leader.

An NDA delegation would meet the President on Friday "if the government dithers on convening a special session of Parliament".

"Our vote would be essentially a show of strength of the NDA alliance," the BJP leader said. Shiv Sena leader Anant Geete, who attended the meeting, said his party's views "were in consonance with the NDA's on the nuclear deal". There were earlier reports that the Maharashtra outfit, along with the Shiromani Akali Dal, might have contradictory views with the NDA on the deal.

A BJP ally present in the meeting, however, sounded a word of caution: "The BJP is very clear on the deal. Even in their debates, they would not like to be seen as against America. In fact, they might not even like the Government to fall on the nuclear deal."

For the BJP, who are preparing for the Lok Sabha elections, the trust vote would then essentially be a display of its alliance's "index of unity" apart from exposing the Congress-SP "opportunistic alliance".

"The Samajwadi Party is misusing the name of former president A P J Abdul Kalam for justifying its midnight U-turn in favour of the nuclear deal and America for their own personal and political interests," said party vice-president Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi.

The NDA meeting was attended by L K Advani, Rajnath Singh and Sushma Swaraj of the BJP, Sharad Yadav, Digvijay Singh of the JD (U), B J Panda and B K Tripathi of the Biju Janata Dal, S S Dhindsa of the Shiromani Akali Dal, Manohar Joshi and Anant Geete of the Shiv Sena among others.

Heading: Cong to make nuclear deal a poll plank - Indian Express
Content:
Soon after a delegation of the Left parties met President Pratibha Patil on Wednesday and formally withdrew its support to the UPA Government, Samajwadi Party leaders Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav drove to Raisina Hills and reiterated their party's support to the Congress-led Government.

"There was some confusion because of certain political differences between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party in the wake of the last Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh. To clear those doubts, we met the President and reiterated the support of the Samajwadi Party to the UPA Government," SP general secretary Amar Singh told reporters.

Dismissing the speculation over the disgruntlement among SP MPs regarding the party's turnaround on the nuclear deal, Amar Singh said the party submitted the list of all its MPs who were elected on SP symbol to the President.

"Names of parliamentarians who fought under the SP symbol are there in the letter and they are bound by the party whip," said Amar Singh, without quoting the exact number in the list.

Officially, the SP has 39 MPs in the Lok Sabha.

Singh said that he had also spoken to rebel party MP Beni Prasad Verma over phone and claimed that the latter had assured his support to the Government on the nuclear deal issue.

"I just spoke to Beni Prasad Yadav and he expressed his support as well as that of Atiq Ahmed," Singh said, adding that the party has also got the support of another MP Baleshwar Yadav who did not participate in the SP meeting on Tuesday.

In addition, another rebel party MP, Raj Babbar, has also indicated his support to the deal, Singh said.

Heading: Muslim bodies launch alliance to ‘thwart’ n-deal - Indian Express
Content:
While the Congress Working Committee (CWC) will meet here on Friday to discuss the situation arising out of the Left's withdrawal of support to the UPA Government, the ruling party on Wednesday braced up to showcase the Indo-US nuclear deal as the UPA Government's attempt towards solving the "basic issues" of bijli, sadak and paani concerning the aam aadmi.

"The nuclear deal is already an electoral issue because in every election bijli, paani and sadak is an issue," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari declared at a press conference here. His remarks marked a significant change in the approach of the ruling party, which was cagey about making an electoral issue out of the deal until recently.

The Congress had chosen to skip any mention of the nuclear deal in its election campaigns. So much was the apprehension in the ruling camp about the electoral implication of the nuclear deal that even AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi, who is known to be in favour of the deal, refrained from making his views public.

But, apparently emboldened by the backing of the deal by many regional parties as also minority organisations and also perhaps left with a fait accompli with the Government deciding to go the whole hog to operationalise the deal, the Congress has now decided to make it an electoral issue in terms of the country's energy requirements.

"In today's situation, all developed and developing nations of the world are keeping their energy options open. By 2050, India is going to be the most populous country. Energy needs of India are going to grow exponentially. Everybody, be it farmers or workers, needs energy. In India's progress the biggest issue is the dearth of energy. For our children, our posterity, energy requirement is the most critical issue. We have, therefore, decided to implement the nuclear deal," said Tewari churning out statistics about the number of nuclear power stations in different countries, including the US, France and Japan.

"Nuclear renaissance is taking place. As many as 35 nuclear plants are being constructed in different parts of the world as of today," said the AICC spokesperson. He said by 2030 India would require 5,00,000 MW of energy as against the current installed capacity of 1,31,000 MW. With the nuclear deal in place, "by 2030, 10 per cent of the gap will come from nuclear power, which will increase to 26 per cent by 2050".

Heading: Fissures in CPM, Bengal minister supports nuke power - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM's attempt to give a "Muslim twist" to the nuclear deal may have backfired, but there seems to be some solace for the Left now that the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind (JIH) — the "ideological face" of Indian Muslims — is in the process of launching a national alliance to fight against imperialism in the light of the Indo-US nuclear deal. As a preliminary to the launch of this alliance, the JIH on Tuesday organised a symposium on the 'Indo-US nuclear deal and national interest' where it was decided, "to oppose the agreement tooth and nail".

The new alliance, which is yet to be named, will be a conglomeration of ideologically compatible Muslim bodies — including All India Muslim Majlis-e-Mushawarat, Indian National League, Muslim Political Council of India and Markazi Jamiat Ulama-e-Hind — as well as a few civil society organisations with strong anti-imperialist leanings such as the Movement for Peace and Justice, Third Freedom Struggle Movement and Rashtriya Samaj Paksh.

Steps towards launching the alliance are already underway, and the first state unit has been formed in Maharashtra with a vow to "thwart the Indo-US nuclear deal and oppose designs of US Imperialism". JIH plans to launch similar units in all states within a month.

Taking a stand that apart from the Left Front no other party is willing to fight against US imperialism, the new alliance has underlined the need to have a joint platform of all Left parties, Socialists, Ambedkarite parties and minority organisations. "A national alliance of anti-imperialist movement is the need of the hour," they say, alleging that the "secular dispensation under Manmohan Singh has sacrificed democratic aspirations on the altar of nuclear agreement" and exhorts "aam admi" to teach "every imperial agent" a lesson in the next election.

"The deal is a covert design to make India subservient to American imperialism. It is not against any particular community or religious group. The entire country's interest is at stake and it must be opposed at all costs," said S Q R Ilyas, member of the Political Committee of JIH. Careful to develop a secular image for the alliance, he added: "Every community is a victim of imperialism and our alliance will have space for everyone who is ready to raise his voice against it."

While maintaining that the new front will have no affiliation to any political parties, leaders of the new coalition do admit that they have an affinity for the Left parties. "It is just a coincidence that we have a similar line that of the Left. We do have serious differences with the Left on several issues but when it comes to opposing imperialism, the Left has always been on the forefront. And we appreciate that," maintained Ilyas.

On whether this would benefit the Left in the next elections, Dr T A Rehmani of the Muslim Political Council of India said: "There is no doubt. It would be mutually beneficial."

Meanwhile, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), a partner in the UPA, has decided to meet on July 10 to decide the party's stand on the nuclear deal after examining all aspects of the issue.

Heading: ‘Amar’s remarks about Sonia demeaning’ - Indian Express
Content:
The fissures in the CPI(M) ranks over the nuclear power issue came to the fore on Wednesday as Nirupam Sen, West Bengal's Minister for Commerce and Industries and CPI(M) Politburo member openly supported nuclear power saying that it was necessary for the country.

"Let me make it very clear that we are not against nuclear power. We want it... It is for the sake of this country that nuclear power is needed," Sen, who also happens to be the latest entrant to the Politburo, said in his chamber at the state assembly lobby.

Sen went on to explain how the state Government had even identified a suitable site for a nuclear power plant at Haripur in East Midnapore. "We were keen on setting up a nuclear power plant at Haripur and a high-level team even visited the place. But then it was the Opposition that threw a spanner in the works and we had to keep it on hold for the time being," the minister said.

Sen said he hoped all projects pending would be cleared. He said in case a new Government comes up at the Centre and the state's projects are opposed by them, it would be most unfortunate and unfair.

Heading: JD(U) MLA, four others killed by Maoists in Jharkhand - Indian Express
Content:
Some women groups demanded an apology from Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh for his reported "sexist" remarks while describe his meeting with Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

Outfits like All India Democratic Women's Association dubbed Singh's remarks as "highly objectionable, condemnable, unacceptable and demeaning to all women".

The Samajwadi Party general secretary had allegedly said in an interview to IANS news agency: "When Prakash Karat goes to meet Sonia Gandhi, it's called 'suhaag raat', but when we go to meet her, it's called 'balaatkaar'."

"It is quite shocking that a political leader can make comments in such bad taste about political relationships that involve a prominent woman leader of the country," women's groups said in a statement.

The statement was issued by AIDWA, National Federation for Indian Women (NFIW), Guild of Service, Centre for Women's Development Studies and Young Women's Christian Association.

Heading: Govt plans guidelines for fertility clinics - Indian Express
Content:
In a bloody attack, CPI(Maoist) guerrillas shot dead a JD(U) MLA and two of his bodyguards, as well as two students, on Wednesday afternoon near Bundu, located along the busy Ranchi-Jamshedpur highway. The incident took place inside the hall of the S S School, just two km from the Bundu police station. As the news spread, shops and market complexes downed shutters throughout the day.

Ex-minister Ramesh Singh Munda, 54, and his three bodyguards — Shiv Nath Minz, Shesh Nath Singh and Khursheed Anwar — had gathered under a pandal along with students and teachers to participate in a function organised by the school to felicitate students who had recently secured first division marks. Incidentally, the school falls in the Tamar (ST) Reserve Assembly constituency, which Munda, who was the chief guest, had represented twice since 2000.

Relating the sequence of events, the school's principal Umesh Dangi said that due to rain, the programme was shifted inside, but before it could recommence, a shabbily dressed man with a flowing beard and hair started screaming in the hall and was eventually driven out. "Soon, two armed extremists entered the school from the main gate. After shooting down Anwar, who stood at the gate with a gun, they started firing indiscriminately. And as the bodyguards fell on the ground, the attackers collected the guns of the deceased men and walked off," said Dangi.

While Munda, Minz, Anwar and two students, who are yet to be identified, died on the spot, Shesh Nath Singh managed to flee the scene. Dangi who was with Munda when the Maoists opened fire told the police that he had watched the bullets hit the politician's forehead, chest and ribs. The bodies were taken to the state Government-run RIMS hospital for post-mortem.

In his confidential report to the DGP in 2006, additional DGP R C Kaithal as IG(CID) had revealed that Munda was on the hit list of the Maoists because he had not paid half of the amount he had promised them in lieu of securing their support during the Assembly polls in 2005.

When asked, DIG R K Mallick told The Indian Express that investigations have started. "The combing operations have begun, but since Bundu and Tamar are surrounded by dense forests and hills across, the security forces were finding it difficult to scan the area," he said. In addition, Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Avinash Kumar and SSP M S Bhatia were camping at the site and reportedly supervising the search operation. By Wednesday evening, a company of the security forces was 'actively deployed' at the school and the state Government's chopper, Dhruv, was pressed into service to facilitate combing operations, said a highly placed source in the police. No arrests have been made so far.

Heading: Plea against SEZ dismissed, petitioners told to approach HC - Indian Express
Content:
The Government on Wednesday assured the Supreme Court that fertility clinics across the country would be regulated by guidelines that would soon be enforced till a suitable Act replaces it.

Terming it as a "serious" issue, Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium attempted to assuage fears of couples being duped by ill-equipped clinics and untrained doctors in clinics.

While hearing an appeal by a couple from Kerala, who was a victim of wrong treatment at a fertility clinic, the Centre's counsel expressed deep concern and submitted that guidelines would be framed for enforcement till the law was made.

"The process of enacting a mandatory law is already on. However, guidelines will be enforced till the law is enacted," he said before the Bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal.

Following the submission, the court granted the Government four weeks to file an affidavit in this regard. The Centre had in its response before the HC submitted the document on 'National Guidelines for Accreditation, Supervision and Regulation of ART Clinics' framed by the Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR).

The couple, aggrieved by the HC's order that had refused to treat their petition as a PIL, has sought framing of guidelines for establishment of infertility clinics, with the method of Assistance Reproductive Technique (ART).

The petitioners had urged that it be treated as a PIL for issuing directions to the Centre for coming out with guidelines for regulating fertility clinics so that others don't undergo the trauma they went through. Due to the negligence of the clinic, a wrong method was applied leading to the mismatch of DNA. As a result, the childless woman had to undergo a major surgery, which had cost them a fortune.

While refusing to treat it as a PIL, the HC had observed that the couple had filed a private lawsuit seeking compensation from the clinic for negligence and deficiency in service.

Heading: Strike over, Jammu returns to normal - Indian Express
Content:
In an apparent departure from its stance of being environment-friendly, the Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to pass any order on a petition filed by a few Gujarat fishermen challenging the Special Economic Zone at Mundra.

In what comes as a breather for the Adani group, the apex court asked the petitioners to approach the respective High Court for directions, if any.

Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan, who heads the "environment bench" in the apex court hearing environment-related matters, however, on Wednesday remarked, "We cannot look into environment issues of each state. You can approach the High Court."

Ironically, the apex court's 'green bench', functioning since 1995, has been looking into environment-related matters of different states across India. The three-member special bench is hearing hundreds of applications seeking environmental clearances for construction or developmental projects.

While refusing to agree with the arguments of senior advocate Rakesh Khanna and Shakil Ahmed Syed, appearing for seven fishermen who alleged irregularities while granting an SEZ to Adani by the Centre and the Gujarat Government, the bench said, "the high courts are the right forum to look into environment matters of the states. How can we do it (look into the issue)?"

The petitioners had approached the apex court fearing irreparable damage to the environment besides their loss of livelihood. On July 1, the bench comprising Justice Altamas Kabir had stayed work on the Rs 7,400-crore multi-product SEZ in Gujarat.

Curiously, in the earlier hearing, the court had even issued notices to the ministries of commerce, and environment and forest, the Gujarat Government, Mundra Ports and Special Economic Zone, the Adani group and others. It had also directed the parties to maintain status quo on all activities taking place in the area.

The court also directed that there should be no destruction of mangrove forests or the creek while allowing dredging operations to keep the port running.

The order was issued after senior counsel Harish Salve, appearing for the Adanis, gave an undertaking before the court that they would not fill up of the creeks.

Heading: VHP calls bandh over ‘attack’ by Christians - Indian Express
Content:
After suspension of the nine-day-long bandh in Jammu, life returned to normal in the city on Wednesday.

Vehicular traffic that had been off the roads due to the agitation rolled on normally even as people returned to their offices. Banks and ATMs witnessed huge rushes as people had to withdraw money for making purchases. All business establishments and commercial units opened, doing brisk business. People were making purchases in large quantities, especially of essential commodities. However most educational institutions remained closed. Reports from other districts like Kathua, Samba, Rajouri stated that people were returning to their normal routines.

The Amarnath Yatra Sangarsh Samiti suspended the bandh on Tuesday "in the interest of the people of Jammu" and gave seven days time to the government to revoke the order. The Samiti has maintained that they will continue their agitation for the removal of Governor N N Vohra and the return of land to Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB).

Meanwhile, Bar Association of Jammu (BAJ), that has decided to continue its strike till Saturday, took out a rally demanding transfer of land back to SASB on Wednesday. Hundreds of lawyers first assembled at High Court premises and showed their resentment against the decision of the Azad government to cancel the land diversion order. Later the protesters took out a car rally, which after passing through various parts of the city, culminated in front of the Governor's residence.

Heading: Stay on EC order to stop work on K’taka expressway - Indian Express
Content:
The tribal-dominated but communally-sensitive Kandhamal district in Orissa on Wednesday witnessed a total bandh by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal in protest against an alleged attack on an inmate of an ashram run by Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati by a few Christians. Christian leaders, on the other hand, alleged that a Jesuit home was attacked in the area.

Schools, colleges and several institutions remained closed for most part of the day as the Sangh Parivar raised the pitch for the sacking of Kandhamal SP Nikhil Kanodia for his partisan activities. State Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik said that the situation is now under control. The State has sent Deputy Inspector General of Police (south-west range) Sanjib Panda and Revenue Divisional Commissioner Satyabrata Sahu to the area for keeping a close watch on the situation.

The district, which was rocked by bloody clashes between Dalit Christians and tribal Hindus in December last year over erection of a gate near a Hindu place of worship, saw another clash on Tuesday when the inmate of an ashram run by the controversial seer and a godman were reportedly assaulted by a few Christians. The godman was reportedly trying to take pictures of slaughtered cows on his cellphone when he was attacked.

Orissa Director General of Police G C Nanda said he will look into the matter if the police have registered any case against people who have been accused of cow slaughter.

Heading: Abandoned girl finds new home, but school asks for birth certificate - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed an Election Commission order which had put on hold the work on the Bangalore-Mysore Expressway Infrastructure Project in Karnataka.

The bench led by Justice Arijit Pasayat also sought a response from the EC besides asking the state Government to express its view on the issue.

The directive had come on a petition by the promoters, Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises (NICE) Development Corporation, who had challenged the May 8, 2008, directive by the EC to stop construction on the project as per the model code of conduct for the May 2008 elections to the state Assembly.

Following a contempt petition by NICE in the apex court in March 2008 accusing the then Gowda government for deliberately coming in the way of the project, a bench had issued contempt notices against the Chief Secretary and other respondents. The cabinet had taken a decision to resume construction.

However, soon after the company started work on the expressway following the apex court directive, the EC issued the May 8 order and construction was stalled. The 111-km expressway connecting Bangalore and Mysore is estimated to cost over Rs 1,500 crore. The stretch would also be dotted by five satellite townships.

Heading: Decision to revise UPSC merit list challenged - Indian Express
Content:
When Rekha Patel, a housemaid, was returning home from work at Adjan, she thought she heard the wails of a newborn infant coming out from a plastic bag that a pack of stray dogs were fighting over in a rubbish bin.

Three years since that evening when Rekha chased away the dogs, held the bleeding infant girl in her arms and ran to the hospital, the child has become a question mark for the state Education department. Re-born in a rubbish bin, she has no birth certificate, and the law says she can't be admitted to a school without it.

After the rescue, Rekha had tended to the infant girl for over a week, at the New Civil hospital, praying she would recover from the dog bites. When she did, no one could tell her what to do with the baby. She had two chronically ailing and unemployed sons in their thirties and an unwell husband back home, all living on whatever meagre income she earned as a housemaid.

But Rekha nevertheless decided to bring up the infant girl as her own. She took her home, called in the neighbours, distributed sweets to announce her new child. While many offered to adopt the infant, she refused. Since she came to her from nowhere, Rekha named the baby Falak (sky) and celebrated every June 14, the day she rescued her from the dogs, as her birthday.

Eager to give her a good education, Rekha approached the trustees of the Nutan School near her home this March, where authorities insisted on the child's birth certificate. They admitted Falak to the school on April 3, but gave Rekha a month's time to get the certificate.

As the deadline approached, someone advised Rekha that she could try for an affidavit in lieu of a birth certificate, but the school rejected it. Even visits to the Surat district panchayat office and later the district primary education office were of no avail. Falak is no longer allowed into the school. District Primary Education Officer P N Dave said he had spoken to the school's trustees and requested them to allow Falak to study and to charge no fees from her. "I also had a talk with a paediatrician and the girl will be taken to his hospital for confirming her age. We will give her a birth certificate after that."

Heading: SC upset over PIL against Bombay HC Chief Justice - Indian Express
Content:
A petition was filed on Wednesday in the Supreme Court against the Union Public Service Commission's (UPSC) decision to revise the result of the Civil Service Examination (CSE)-2007 by deleting names of 96 reserved category candidates from the general list and adding their names to the quota list.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishanan did not pass any order on the plea by 12 reserved category candidates to restrain UPSC from issuing appointment letters to successful candidates but agreed to hear the petition on an urgent basis on July 18.

The revised provisional list was published after the apex court on May 19 had stayed the Madras HC decision setting aside the merit list prepared by the UPSC. The court on March 20 had quashed Rule 16(2) of the CSE by holding it as 'null and void' saying that it ran counter to the benefit of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and OBC candidates and was not affirmative, progressive and pragmatic in achieving social justice.

The petitioners contended that the two Constitution Benches of the apex court, in their earlier judgements, had said that a reserved category candidate selected in general merit list cannot be counted in the reserved category to tally with the total number of seats allocated to them.

Heading: US panel opposes visa to Modi - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday took strong exception to a public interest litigation (PIL) by two Mumbai-based advocates alleging that the Chief Justice of Bombay High Court favoured those who belonged to his community during the transfer of judges in the subordinate judiciary.

After hearing the petition, the bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan said action must be taken against the advocates. The bench issued a limited notice to the state Government to know why action should not be taken against the advocates for "professional misconduct".

Heading: 22 dogs found dead in Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
A US government advisory agency has asked the State Department not to reverse its decision to deny a tourist visa to Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi for allegedly abetting human rights violations.

"The Commission on International Religious Freedom again urges the State Department to announce Modi's ineligibility for a visa under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). We have not seen changes that would warrant a policy reversal," said the federal agency's Chairman Felice D Gaer.

Modi was invited last month to attend a Gujarati culture conference in New Jersey, to be held in August. Earlier in 2005, Modi was denied entry into the US to attend the same conference citing his role as the Chief Minister during the 2002 Gujarat riots.

Heading: Left alone, PMK eyes allies - Indian Express
Content:
At least 22 dogs were found dead in Nerul on Wednesday morning. The Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation suspects that they were poisoned.

The Nerul police registered a case against unknown persons based on a complaint from Renu Rai, an animal rights activist who also heads an NGO that takes care of canines. Rai said she feared that the dogs were poisoned.

"Last night, I saw some dogs looking ill and gave them medicines. But around 6 am, I got a call from someone who said that dogs had died in Army Colony and State Bank of India Colony in Nerul. Some 22 dogs were found dead at different places with blood oozing from their mouth," Rai said.

Heading: She left her Karnataka home for work and money; 3 yrs on, found dead in Goa village - Indian Express
Content:
The Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), after being in alliances with both the DMK and the AIADMK in the State, has decided to forge an alliance that can take on both the Dravidian parties for the coming general elections.

Interestingly, PMK founder S Ramadoss, who made this announcement at Ramanathapuram on Tuesday, has said that Congress would lead the alliance front in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. He, however, did not elaborate on this. Senior leaders said that the party was looking at all options that can take on its rivals.

On Monday night, Ramadoss had stated that the days of 'minority DMK Government was numbered in the state.' PMK was a part of an alliance with the DMK till being thrown out on charges of functioning against the alliance dharma.

PMK, highly critical of the State Government since its formation, has increased its pitch following the snapping of ties and arrest of senior leader J Guru, and has revived the pet theme of the Ramadoss family: prohibition. Conferences demanding eradication of liquor are being held in districts one by one starting from Monday, directly taking on the Government for its liquor policies.

At one point in the past - when PMK was still an 'ally' - when he urged Chief Minister M Karunanidhi to enforce prohibition in the state, an irritated Karunanidhi retorted saying that Ramadoss can enforce total prohibition when his party comes to power. Though the 'if' part was avoided in his reply, the implication that PMK was still a minor political party was not missed.

Even while they don't rule out a change in alliance dynamics in theory, DMK leaders here do not believe that the Congress, in need of support from anyone and everyone to continue in the Centre for another year, will pull the plug for some more time. "This statement by Ramadoss, if made at any other point of time, would have generated greater interest. At this juncture, when the Union Government is facing a crisis, we are almost certain that the Congress will not take a step that would disturb the present relations," contended a DMK member.

There are also rumours about Congress moving closer to smaller parties like actor-politician Vijayakanth's DMDK. Adding credibility to the rumours, AICC in charge for Tamil Nadu, Arunkumar had reportedly met Vijayakanth on board a domestic flight that irked the DMK high brass.

Though the Congress-PMK-DMDK alliance looks strong on calculation and statistics, there are still differences between DMDK and the PMK. To put things in perspective, DMDK was floated after the matinee star launched a tirade against Ramadoss for making his 'inexperienced son a Rajya Sabha member and a cabinet minister.' According to sources in PMK, 'Captain' had turned his attention to DMK and AIADMK, declaring that he was open to alliance with other parties.

Also, PMK is a staunch supporter of the LTTE cause, an ever-irritating issue for the Congress leaders here, though it did not create any problems in sharing power at the Centre.

To Congress' credit, though ousted from power in the State decades ago by DMK, the vote bank that it commands decides which party would rule Tamil Nadu. The present State Government led by M Karunanidhi has only 96 MLAs in a house of 234, and is propped up by 35-members of the Congress.

Heading: IIT theme: tech that helps common man - Indian Express
Content:
Three years ago, Moitheenkunhi was filled with fresh hopes for his young daughter. "The people of Kasargod are very rich and caring. My client will give you money to marry off your daughter," the farm worker at Ayyankeri in Karnataka's Kodagu district, was told when his only daughter Safiya was handed over to Moithu Haji, a broker who arranged domestic servants for the rich.

That was on June 15, 2005.

The deal finalised, Safiya, then 14, was brought to the house of K C Hamza, near Kasargod, in North Kerala. In the meanwhile, the adolescent's parents waited for their daughter's return, convinced she'd come loaded with money and gold.

But three years into that dream, the distraught father last week found that his daughter would not come back, either alive or dead. Moitheenkunhi stood on the sidelines in a Goan village-where the Kerala police had taken him-and witnessed his daughter's mortal remains being exhumed. And from the evidence that police have unearthed so far, there was nothing quick and painless about Safiya's death; it is likely that she was tortured and exploited for several months.

The mystery behind Safiya's 'disappearance' was solved last week, when investigators from the crime branch of the police arrested Hamza, his wife Mymoona, Hamza's aide Abdulla and broker Moithu Haji, on charges of murdering the girl after subjecting her to a litany of horrors.

"The investigation is still in progress. We have gathered evidence to substantiate that the girl was gangraped, before being killed," police sources said.

Relating the incidents that led to the murder, police said in October 2006, Hamza, a contractor, had taken Safiya, whom he had employed as a domestic worker, to Goa, where he had then undertaken the construction of a small dam.

Three months later, Hamza and his family came back to Kasargod, but when Moitheenkunhi rushed to meet his daughter, he was informed that Safiya had gone missing in Goa. Although a complaint was filed at the local police station in Kasargod,the matter quickly came to naught-while a police team went to Goa, it returned without any leads in the case.

Meanwhile, Hamza went about his business, but it wasn't long before people's opinion started turning against him, with the 'missing' theory being brought into question. With the support of local political leaders and social organisations, Moitheenkunhi and his wife staged a sit-in in front of the district superintendent of police in Kasargod on November 12, 2007. This agitation turned into a mass movement after an action committee was formed, demanding an impartial probe into the missing girl incident.

Amidst mounting protest from the public, the state Government handed over the case to the crime branch in April 2008. In a matter of months the team discovered attempts made by the local police to cover up the case.

Upon questioning, Hamza revealed to the police that Safiya had suffered burn injuries during cooking, claiming that he kept her within his house, instead of rushing to a hospital. While she was battling for her life, Hamza added, he cut her body into three pieces. He then proceeded to pack the body parts into a bag, which was thrown into a pit, near the site of the dam under construction. However, police sources say that this is not the complete truth about the murder-which is believed to have taken place about a year and a half ago-and that several other accomplices may be involved.

"Hamza's version could not be believed. It has to be suspected that many others were also involved in the murder of the girl," the sources said. It is hoped that forensic examinations of the victim's remains will reveal more details about the crime.

Heading: Former Kerala minister summoned to court over scribe’s molestation - Indian Express
Content:
When the young and upcoming engineers shift their attention from the mouse to mosquito zappers, it could pave the way for a healthy tomorrow.

Shaastra, the technical festival of the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras, has asked engineering students to come up with technological solutions to many of the common problems faced by the public across India.

To celebrate the golden jubilee year of Shaastra, the organisers have come up with innovative programmes that test the problem solving capability of students under the 'Golden Design Challenges'. Turning its attention from high-end technology to the common man's problems, one of the five Golden Challenges is to build an effective model of a mosquito control device that would help control vector-borne diseases efficiently under various public health initiatives.

Another challenge is to invent a device that can purify drinking water to the maximum extent with minimum expense.

Other interesting projects that the students could participate in include developing a robot that would be able to sort books in a library and place them in their respective shelves with the help of an overhead camera.

Shaastra 2008, the only ISO 9001-2000 certi-fied students' event in the world, will be held from October 1 to 5.

Heading: Jharkhand Govt not to acquire ICAR land - Indian Express
Content:
Former Kerala minister and leader of a Congress faction, PJ Joseph, was on Wednesday directed by the Alandur Judicial Magistrate to appear before the court on Thursday for his involvement in a molestation case.

The victim — a presenter in a private news channel — had alleged that Jospeh had molested her on board a private airline in 2006.

Joseph had pleaded with the court to exempt him from appearing in person citing health reasons. The magistrate, however, refused to entertain the request and directed him to appear for the next hearing. Joseph, founder of the regional party Kerala Congress (Joseph), is facing charges under Section 354 of the IPC and Tamil Nadu Prevention of Women Harassment Act.

The allegations were later substantiated prima facie by a senior woman police officer from Kerala and Joseph was forced to resign as PWD minister from the LDF Government.

His name was back to the reckoning after his successor, T U Kuruvilla, was also forced to step down unceremoniously after facing allegations of helping his children in a real estate deal, though the alliance partners refused to entertain his claims till he was acquitted from the case.

Heading: LS Secretariat open to public scrutiny - Indian Express
Content:
The move to acquire land from ICAR's Ranchi-based Horticulture & Agro Forestry Research Programme (HARP) for a housing scheme for MPs and MLAs has been shelved. "We do not want to get into a land dispute," Jharkhand Assembly Speaker Alamgir Alam said on Wednesday.

It was The Indian Express that first reported on October 4, 2007, the move to acquire 88 acres of HARP land for bungalow plots. This had set off a chain reaction, with HARP's Principal Scientist Dr Shivendra Kumar threatening to move court and Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar asking Chief Minister Madhu Koda to keep off from the land.

Till recently, Koda and Alam had preferred to remain mum on the issue. But with clouds of uncertainty hovering over the UPA Government at the Centre and the state, they have been working overtime for land acquisition elsewhere. Three plots of government land measuring nearly 80 acres in the outskirts of Ranchi has been shortlisted, which will provide accommodation to over 200 politicians, including the state's 82 MLAs and 20 MPs. Ranchi Deputy Collector (Land Reforms) Kartik K Prabhat confirmed that the plots were clear of encroachment. "It is 100 per cent encroachment-free government land," said Prabhat.

On July 3, Alam presided over a meeting attended by a dozen government functionaries, apart from Koda and Prabhat, where it was resolved to expedite the latest land acquisition process. "The move is in the interest of every legislator and MP," said C P Singh, principal opposition party BJP's chief whip.

Incidentally, while several key Greenfield projects including those proposed by Naveen Jindal, L N Mittal and Ratan Tata have been stalled for years because of the Koda Government's minimal efforts to get them any land, there is no opposition to the new land acquisition for constructing bungalows for MLAs' and MPs'.

Heading: Chhattisgarh suggests PPP model to improve school education - Indian Express
Content:
In a first, the Central Information Commission (CIC) directed a private person to "personally inspect" documents regarding recruitment and filling up of vacancies to various posts in the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

The decision on Monday made clear that every citizen had right to know "how his tax money is used in larger public interest to service the people's elected representatives and the Parliament".

The Secretariat had tried to fend off the supply of the information by saying the exercise under RTI was an unnecessary diversion of "time, expense and manpower resources" to cull out the specific data sought from computerised records.

"Records of vacancies and recruitment are computerised and automatically updated by the computer. Therefore, seeking to find separate information in the specific form, in which it is asked for, would involve time, expense and the diversion of manpower resources," reasoned Deputy Secretary, Lok Sabha Secretariat, to the listening CIC Bench.

In reply, the Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah observed that information under RTI cannot be denied merely on the ground that data was in a computerised format.

To save the Secretariat from any bother, the Bench said the applicant himself could approach the Secretariat authorities within the next 20 days and personally check the records at their offices.

Vinod Babu of Dharam Marg in Chanakyapuri had appealed to the topmost transparency panel after the Secretariat denied him access to information on the number of posts lying vacant for the past 10 years from the period between1997 to 2006.

Heading: Denied bail, Gorkha bandh-hit Czech scientists in jail till July 21 - Indian Express
Content:
Recognising the general aversion to government schools, the Chhattisgarh Government is looking at taking the Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) route to improve education in the state.

A draft of the state's proposed new school education policy, which takes a dim view of the present scenario, suggests this as among other innovative measures needed to streamline the system. The policy, however, does not elaborate on the concept.

The draft policy lists non-enrollment of children in schools, alarming dropout rates, inadequate number of high schools and higher secondary schools, untrained teachers and the absence of a policy for English education as among the problems plaguing the system.

However, the opposition Congress is sceptical about the PPP move. "The acrobatic language used in the draft policy about a PPP model itself indicates that the BJP Government wants to hide something about the concept," says state Congress working president Satyanarayan Sharma, a former school education minister.

Heading: Matka king’s murder: cops track down son in Goa, arrest him - Indian Express
Content:
The bail petition of Czech entomologist Petr Svacha, and his associate, Emil Kucera, arrested on June 22 for allegedly collecting specimens of rare insects from Singalila National Park, was rejected for the second time on Wednesday and their judicial remand was extended till July 21.

Svacha, 51, and Kucera, 52, had personally submitted a petition before the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court asking the court to open for a day so that their bail plea could be heard. In response to their petition, a "special hearing" was held in the CJM's court, but they were denied bail, said Divisional Forest Officer Sumita Ghatak. "The JC period would be used for investigation and questioning," he added.

The Czech entomologists have not been able to muster enough legal assistance because of an indefinite cease-work by Darjeeling lawyers and a strike in Government offices across the hills, including the district court.

Svacha, a biologist with Czech Academy of Sciences and Kucera, a forestry specialist, were held by the Forest Department with nearly 200 specimens of rare insects, both full-grown and in larva stage.

"They were arrested from a hotel near the National Park following a tip-off. They had collected Schedule-I butterflies and rare species of beetles, moths, larvae and pupae. The insects, classified as Schedule-I, belong to the extremely rare category and collecting them from a National Park without permission or authorisation is a non-bailable offence under the Wildlife Protection Act," Ghatak said.

A petition signed by over 500 scientists from India asking Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee for their release has not helped their cause. The Czech Embassy has been in touch with both the External Affairs Ministry and the Darjeeling district administration but nothing has happened so far.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Czech Acting Consul Yan Kreuter said he had visited both entomologists in jail last Monday. "They are not young anymore. They have been kept with other detainees in the same cell under poor conditions," said Kreuter.

Heading: ULFA cadres in ‘ceasefire’ ask for designated camps - Indian Express
Content:
Officers of the Crime Branch arrested Hitesh Bhagat, son of 'matka king' Suresh Bhagat and Jaya Bhagat, from Goa where he had gone into hiding after the police started looking for him for his possible involvement in the conspiracy behind the murder of his father on June 13.

According to the Crime Branch, Hitesh Bhagat was also involved in the conspiracy in which Suresh's former wife Jaya had conspired with Suhas Roge, an Arun Gawli aide, to eliminate Suresh and take over the multi-crore 'matka' business.

Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said: "Hitesh, who was the co-accused along with Suresh in the narcotics case at Alibaug, was a key conspirator in the conspiracy to murder Suresh Bhagat. He had been present at one of the meetings between Roge and Jaya at the latter's residence, where they had met to discuss the murder conspiracy."

Maria said Hitesh had fled to Goa on July 4 and had been staying at Hotel Sun N Sand in Panaji. "We had received information that Hitesh was there. Our team went to Goa and arrested him and brought him back to Mumbai. We also recovered Rs 11 lakh from him," said Maria.

On June 13, Bhagat and six others were murdered in an orchestrated accident on the Alibaug-Pen road near Shahabaz village. A truck had collided head-on with the Scorpio they were travelling in. Police investigations revealed that a 'supari' of Rs 45 lakh had been paid for the murder.

Further investigations revealed that Jaya, who was suspected to be in a relationship with Roge, had been the one who had orchestrated the 'accident'. Before his death, Bhagat had filed an application with the Crime Branch stating that he feared bodily harm from Jaya, Hitesh and Roge, and that they were trying to frame him in false cases. He had also alleged that Jaya and Roge wanted to take over his assets.

Heading: Ramadoss promises National School Health Programme in three months - Indian Express
Content:
Over 200 ULFA cadres who had joined a unilateral 'ceasefire' under Mrinal Hazarika — self-styled commander of the outfit's 28th battalion — defying the top leadership, have asked the Government to establish two designated camps for them at Lakhipathar and Chapakhowa in Upper Assam where they can stay under the protection of security forces.

"We declared ceasefire in the larger interest of facilitating a peaceful settlement of our issues. Since the Government has so far given positive signals towards our gesture, it should now set up two designated camps for our cadres," Hazarika, who was only recently released from jail, said on Wednesday. Hazarika and his two trusted aides — Jiten Dutta and Jon Sonowal, self-styled commanders of the 'A' and 'C' companies of the 28th battalion that was involved in killing Hindi-speaking people in Upper Assam last year — also organised a public meeting at Kakopathar in Tinsukia district on Tuesday with the Government indirectly facilitating it.

Those present at the meeting included villagers from Kakopathar, local Congress leader Ratneswar Moran and AGP's local unit president Nirmal Bora and a local Vaishnavite satradhikar, Srikumar Goswami.

Interestingly, Kakopathar, eastern-most area of Assam, has a very strong ULFA influence since its formation in 1979. It was at Lakhipathar, close to Kakopathar, that the ULFA had its general headquarters till the outfit was declared illegal and Army was deployed to tackle them in November 1990.

"We have violated ULFA's discipline to declare a unilateral ceasefire in the interest of Assam and Assamese people. We don't mind being expelled from the organisation for that," Hazarika said. The group would look forward to a peaceful settlement of the ULFA's demand, he added.

What is most significant is that the group has sought expulsion of Bangladeshi migrants from Assam. "Unabated influx of Bangladeshis as well as migration of people from rest of India has threatened the very existence of the indigenous population of Assam. Various tribal communities have also drifted away from the Assamese-speaking people. This is a very serious issue," Hazarika said.

Heading: Congress soft towards ISI, Bangla migrants in Assam: AASU - Indian Express
Content:
An ambitious National School Health Programme (NSHP) would be launched within two or three months focusing on prevention of a number of diseases among children across the country.

Disclosing this, Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss said that over two lakh school teachers across the country have been imparted training on various aspects of healthcare, and they have already helped screen the health of over 2.5 crore students in the past one year or more. "Our focus is on looking at eyesight, heart, skin and dental care of school children, and once a considerable level of awareness is generated among school children about these areas, the overall health scenario of the nation would automatically go up," Ramadoss, who was speaking at a seminar on disability organized by 'Dristidaan', a Guwahati-based NGO , for the visually impaired on Tuesday said.

The Union Health Minister said that of the 2.5 crore school children already screened, over 11 lakh have been found to have refraction problems, while over three lakh were provided with glasses for correction of their eyesight. "A large percentage of children are also anaemic," he added.

Speaking about integrating the National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB) with the school health programme, Ramadoss said that a goal has already been set to reduce prevalence of blindness from the existing 1.4 per cent to 0.3 per cent by 2020. "As per the latest survey conducted in 2006-07, prevalence of blindness has already come down to one per cent," he said.

Ramadoss said that besides addressing age-related problems like cataract, glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy, the Government was equally concerned about visual impairment and blindness in children and young adults. "Restoring vision in a visually disabled child would mean a gain of 50 to 60 productive years to his or her life," he said, adding that the Government was open to sharing responsibilities of paediatric ophthalmology and eye-banking with the private sector.

Heading: Mumbai riots: former Sena MP Sarpotdar, 2 others get year in jail - Indian Express
Content:
The All Assam Students' Union (AASU) hit out at the Congress governments at the Centre and in the state for being "soft" and "indifferent" towards the increasing threat from Bangladeshi infiltrators, the ISI and various fundamentalist forces.

"Bangladeshi infiltrators, ISI agents and fundamentalist forces having links with the two are thriving just because they have the blessings of the Congress party. All these forces in return want the Congress to remain in power so that their dream of merger of Assam and the Northeast into a Greater Bangladesh is realised," AASU advisor Samujjal Bhattacharyya said at a press conference on Wednesday.

The AASU tirade against the Congress came on the eve of the third anniversary of the Supreme Court quashing the notorious Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, popularly known as the IMDT Act. The student body asked the Government for an Action-Taken Report on the directives given in 2005 by the apex court while scrapping the Act.

"The Supreme Court, which had taken strong exception to the government's lackadaisical attitude towards the dangerous designs behind the large-scale infiltration from Bangladesh, had also laid down a set of guidelines for the Central and state Governments. But both Delhi and Dispur have done precious little to honour the apex court and safeguard the integrity and sovereignty of the country, apart from saving the people of Assam from being wiped out," AASU general secretary Tapan Kumar Gogoi said at the press conference.

The student leaders highlighted the recent release of seven ISI agents which includes two Pakistanis and a Bangladeshi national, from prisons in Assam. They said these men, arrested during the AGP's tenure in 1999, were freed at the instance of the Congress-led Government.

"The Government had earlier failed to even express any concern when another ISI operative escaped from custody two years ago," the AASU leader said.

Heading: Nuclear deal crucial to meet India’s energy needs: Kakodkar - Indian Express
Content:
Sixteen years after the Mumbai riots in the wake of the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, a special court on Wed- nesday sentenced senior Shiv Sena leader and former MP Madhukar Sarpotdar and two others to one-year simple imprisonment for making an inflammatory speech to incite violence. Sarpotdar is the first senior Shiv Sena leader to be convicted for involvement in the riots.

Magistrate Rajeshwari Bapat-Sarkar convicted Sarpotdar and two Shiv Sainiks — Ashok Shinde and Jaywant Parab — under Section 153 (A) of the Indian Penal Code. They were also fined Rs 5,000 each. They were later granted bail, on a bond of Rs 5,000 each, until August 16 after which they will be taken into custody. The trio will appeal in the Bombay High Court against the conviction.

The court acquitted three others accused in the same case — Umesha Pawar, Pradeep Khanvilkar and Shantaram Sadvantar.

After being convicted, Sarpotdar said he was ready to face imprisonment and was not afraid to go to jail. "The prosecution has not produced any evidence against me but I will read the whole judgment and then appeal against it," he said.

"Every political activist enters the domain of politics only after making up his mind. I have never been called a hardened criminal, but am used to going to jail time and again. My 40-year political career has made me sound, both physically and mentally, to take such judgments easily," he said.

Sarpotdar was accused of leading a mob of more than 5,000 people from the Ganesh Utsav Samiti Mandal in Bandra on December 27, 1992. According to the chargesheet, Sarpotdar led the mob, chanting slogans like "Mandir yahin banega" and "Yahan pe rehna hoga toh Vande Mataram kehna hoga." The chargesheet also made mention of several derogatory words used against the Muslim community.

Though the incident occurred on December 27, 1992 an FIR was lodged only two days later. Following delay in locating witnesses, the chargesheet was filed in 1994.

"Throughout the case, the prosecution could not rely on the witnesses. While one witness, Pandurang Tayde, a constable then in-charge of patrolling, claimed to have lost memory in an accident, another witness, then Police Inspector Mohan Khanolkar, appeared in court only after numerous summons and a bailable warrant. It was a state case, hence the state machinery should have been proactive," said Additional Public Prosecutor M S Kadam.

Heading: Centre working on laws to prevent immigration scams - Indian Express
Content:
Mounting possibly his strongest defence yet of the Indo-US nuclear co-operation agreement, Atomic Energy Commission chairman Anil Kakodkar on Wednesday said India was negotiating the pact from a position of strength and called attempts to isolate the country's nuclear programme from the world "foolish".

Armed with a brief powerpoint presentation for a panel discussion, Kakodkar said he wanted to put the controversial deal in "proper perspective". While India's indigenous programme had achieved much both in the civilian and military sectors, global co-operation was needed now to meet the country's soaring energy needs and bridge the supply gap, he said.

"Let there be no fear that we are attempting civil nuclear co-operation from a position of weakness or from a donor-recipient position," the AEC chairman said. "We are talking of engaging the world from a strong business position, from a position of India's power requirements both in the short-term and the long-term. So that we can bridge the energy security gap that we foresee."

Meticulously explaining the charts in his presentation, Kakodkar said India's power requirement is forecast at 1,300 Gigawatts by 2050 and there would be a shortage of about 400 Gigawatts without the nuclear deal. A 10-year delay in operationalising the deal would lead to a shortfall of about 180 Gigawatts, he added.

India's three-stage nuclear programme would not need international help in perpetuity, Kakodkar said, attempting to allay fears of some sections that New Delhi would be bound to global powers forever under the deal. "If civil nuclear co-operation opens up and we are able to import 40 Gigawatts of nuclear power production capability between 2012 and 2020, the deficit projected in 2050 will practically be wiped out," he said.

"Some people might say what is the big deal in an additional 40 Gigawatts but 40 Gigawatts is 40 Gigawatts," he said and added that fuel imported and used during this period could be recycled for the future while the fast-breeder reactors would also pitch in.

He said he was not opposed to the deal in the initial stages as perceived but admitted that he had reservations about some negotiation positions involving securing reprocessing rights and not placing the fast-breeder reactors under safeguards and those had been taken care of. "There were issues that had to be insisted," he said.

Asked about the opposition to the deal by some Indian nuclear scientists who had been his colleagues, Kakodkar replied: "I have heard various viewpoints but on the question whether the country needs power or not, I have not heard a second view."

The debate over India's nuclear programme brought to mind "our own development as men and women", Kakodkar said. "When you are a small baby, you have all the protection from external influences. But once you grow into an adult it would be foolish to stay protected. If a growing adult is prevented from interacting with the world, he will become lame."

Heading: Governor suspends UP CIC - Indian Express
Content:
The Government is finally taking strong legislative measures to curb the malaise of illegal immigration, human trafficking and frequent deportations of Indian migrants. An ordinance has been finalised — the draft was sent to the Union Cabinet last week and is awaiting approval -- for amending the 1983 Emigration Act to include provisions to prohibit illegal emigration and human smuggling and making punishments more stringent.

The note for the Cabinet prepared by the Ministry of NRI Affairs states that the Ordinance was "a paradigm shift and a comprehensive review of the existing legislative processes in the light of past experience".

Also that following major immigration scams such as the ones in Mississippi involving 500 Indian recruits and the February 2007 incident in Spain which led to deportation of 300 Indians, there was an urgency to show a "strong signal and commitment of the Government to curb acts of human smuggling and illegal immigration".

Among the important provisions of the Ordinance which has the approval of the Ministries of Legal Affairs, Home Affairs and Finance are:

• The strengthening of criterion for registration of recruitment agencies and the deposit fee for them to be increased from the existing Rs 1 lakh to Rs 10 lakh. Specific provisions are being included for renewal and cancellation of registration certificates.

• New clause in the 1983 Act has been proposed to prohibit illegal emigration and human smuggling. Thus, a new offence under the title "human smuggling" is being inserted to deal with intermediaries and recruiting agencies assisting or abetting illegal entry into a country.

• Penalties for violations of the Act are proposed to be enhanced to imprisonment for five years as against the existing two years and a fine of Rs 1 lakh instead of the existing Rs 2,000.

• At the same time, another new provision enables the Central Government to take measures to safeguard interests of emigrants and for Indian diplomatic missions to enquire about their working conditions.

On the administrative side, the ordinance aims to appoint Deputy Protector General of Emigrants who will be empowered for regulating the functioning of recruitment agencies and blacklisting erring employers. The note for the Cabinet mentions that since 2006, the Protector General of Emigrants has received 78 complaints of illegal recruitment of Indians abroad and that 21 of these cases resulted in grant of sanction for prosecution.

Heading: Health is wealth for insurance giants - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Governor T V Rajeswar on Wednesday suspended the state's Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) M A Khan for alleged misconduct and grave irregularities in some appointments. Khan was not allowed in his office. The Governor also initiated the process for CIC's removal by making a reference to the Supreme Court for holding an inquiry into the charges against him.

Under Section 17 of the RTI Act, the CIC can be removed by the Governor for proven misbehaviour or incapacity after the Supreme Court, in an inquiry made on the Governor's reference, has found the charges true and held that he can be removed. A note, issued by the Chief Secretary's office, said there were complaints about Khan's working style, in violation of Right To Information (RTI) Act, 2005. He also interfered in the functioning of other officials of the commission. Khan could not be reached for comment.

Heading: Infrastructure growth falls sharply this year - Indian Express
Content:
Post de-tariffing, if fire and engineering are making holes in the balance sheets of non-life insurance companies, it is the retail business — health and motor — that is raking in the moolah. The two sectors account for almost two-third of the Rs 28,126.4 crore general insurance industry.
