Content: Orissa said it would rethink the inclusion of Above Poverty Line (APL) families living in KBK (Kalahandi-Balangir-Koraput) region as beneficiaries of rice at Rs two per kg scheme.Food and Civil Supplies Minister Manmohan Samal said "The government has decided to provide subsidised rice to all till strategy to exclude APL families is ready".

Heading: Cops refusing to file FIRs should be taken to task: SC to state govts - Indian Express
Content:
The supreme court on Monday reached a "unanimous" agreement that the infamous UP provident fund scam, unearthed from a Ghaziabad court recently allegedly involving several sitting and retired judges, needed to be probed thoroughly.

Following in-chamber deliberations that took place as ordered earlier, a Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan said further hearing in the matter would be held in an open court on July 17.

The Adhivakta Kalyan Trust, Ghaziabad, and Bar Association of Ghaziabad had sought a judicial probe into the corruption case. They referred to an FIR involving withdrawal of crores of rupees from the provident fund account of third- and fourth-grade employees in Ghaziabad region between 2001 and 2008.

However, on Saturday, another petition by Transparency International was filed, which opposed the idea of holding a probe into the scam by a retired or sitting judge of the apex court and instead sought an "unfettered probe".

The organisation submitted that a judicial probe would not only be against the Code of Criminal Procedure but would further strengthen the growing public perception that judiciary appears to be closing ranks to prevent any investigation into the scam.

During the last hearing, senior advocate Fali S Nariman, appearing for the lawyers' bodies, had described the scam as a "serious matter." The scam in which names of 26 members of judiciary, including an apex court judge and seven Allahabad High Court judges, had cropped up could not be probed either by the police or the CBI, he contended.

Heading: Size of 1993 blasts case records fastforwards SC into computer age - Indian Express
Content:
Venting its anger at the police who refuse to register FIRs, the Supreme Court on Monday issued notices to all state governments and the Centre to ensure that the police personnel who find reasons not to register cases on the basis of complaints are not let off.

The Bench comprising Justices B N Aggrawal and G S Singhvi directed all Director Generals of Police and Commissioners of Police to file their responses within three weeks and adjourned the matter for further hearing to August 8.

Underlining the requirement to have such guidelines in place, the court deplored the fact that despite repeated judgments from the apex court, there have been several cases where the police have refused to register FIRs. "Such guidelines were essential to ensure that the erring officers were prosecuted and sent to jail for neglecting duty," it said, taking a strict view of the lackadaisical policing in the country.

The direction came on a habeas corpus petition filed by one Bhola Kamat, whose 16-year-old daughter was allegedly abducted by a few people over a land dispute. Kamat claims to have filed a complaint with the local police, who allegedly threatened him to withdraw it and enter into a compromise with the accused, including an advocate. "Its a disturbing state of affairs," the Bench observed while asking the accused and the Uttar Pradesh Police to file their detailed reply on the allegations.

Advocate Pranesh appearing for the petitioner told the court that Kamat's daughter Lalita Kumar, a resident of Ilaichipur village in UP's Ghaziabad district, was kidnapped by some persons at the alleged instance of the said advocate. The girl is yet to be traced.

According to Kamat, he lodged a complaint with the local police who failed to register an FIR following which he submitted a representation to the SSP Ghaziabad.

Heading: No guidelines for CAG appointment: Court - Indian Express
Content:
Prompted by voluminous records in the 1993 blasts case, the Supreme Court, for the first-time, is likely to witness the use of laptops and computers during the hearing of appeals against the trial court judgment.

The advocates appearing from both sides — the convicts who have challenged their conviction and the sentence, and the investigating agency — would be seen using their laptops. The evidence and numerous case citations would be stored in the CD-Roms. These CDs would then, if required, be given to the judges.

Even the Bench would also be seen with computer screens in their front and everything they wish to know about the case or even the previous judgments, would be available at the touch of a button.

All this is likely to happen in August when the appeals may be listed for hearing.

The suggestion came during the hearing of a convict, Yusuf Abdul Razak Memon, who was sentenced to life by a TADA court. He had sought extension of interim bail granted to him on February 29 after his medical report confirmed he was suffering from schizophrenia and needed a supportive environment which could not be provided in jail.

Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan appeared in agreement with senior advocate Harish Salve who said it would not be feasible for the court to go through voluminous case records as just the evidence runs into thousands of pages. "Citing a case law and taking it out for court's perusal would not be that simple. With so many appeals being filed, we don't think it would be possible to have more than four cases cited," he added.

Salve pointed out, "Special TADA judge P D Kode has already done it so meticulously."

The CJI, sitting with Justice P Sathasivam, said the registrar-general would be told to find out how this could be made possible.

Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium, who appears for CBI, too appeared positive about the novel proposal.
